method: Independent full-content inspection of all 198 assigned current files, including every core/gateway implementation and assigned test, all web components/hooks/libraries/tests, styles, configuration and assigned documentation. Truncated source reads were supplemented. Traced current authorization/CSRF, exact connection ownership and cancellation, durable operation state transitions and unknown outcomes, UI draft/recovery workflows, request/response/resource budgets and routing contracts. Followed current MCP runtime/schema callsites for the reported media boundary. Ran only three specifically justified targeted test files plus a static-render/header and bounded streaming compression-count probe; no prior audit conclusions were used as correctness evidence.

findings.title: MCP tool images bypass decoded-media budgets and load automatically
findings.description: McpContent trusts a declared image MIME type, a permissive Base64 character regex and a 1,400,000-character bound, then immediately emits an img with a data URL for every image entry. It never applies mediaBytes/mediaMime, reads image dimensions, limits total preview pixels or requires a separate preview action. McpPanel renders retained tool content immediately. A connected tool can therefore return a compact, schema-valid image that fits all serialized-byte caps but exceeds the existing 40,000,000-pixel policy and drives excessive browser decode memory/CPU. Multiple images also receive src simultaneously. This can freeze or terminate the active browser tab and disrupt unsaved work. The audit demonstrated missing guards and size feasibility; it did not decode a large image or reproduce an actual OOM.

evidence.observation: Only MIME/encoded-string checks precede automatic img creation; map has no preview count or pixel budget.
Accepted tool result is read into the attempt and its content is rendered through McpContent without an explicit image-preview control.
Body retention is capped at 2 MiB of UTF-8 JSON, which does not bound image dimensions or decoded memory.
Native MCP result validation checks the protocol schema and serialized historyBytes cap (8 MiB); it has no image-header/pixel validation.
Tool content is Array<JsonValue>; the official result contract does not supply a decoded-media budget.
Existing shared helpers enforce Base64/byte validity, PNG/GIF/WebP/JPEG signatures/dimensions, dimensions <=16,384 per side, positive dimensions and <=40,000,000 pixels; MCP does not call them.
Other message media requires an explicit load/preview action before assigning an image src.

reproduction: Load the current McpContent and mediaMime modules with Vite SSR and render McpContent with React renderToStaticMarkup only; no browser or raster decoder is involved.

Supply a 24-byte synthetic PNG header with IHDR width=12000 and height=12000. McpContent emits one img with data:image/png;base64 src. mediaMime rejects the same 144,000,000-pixel header. The tool-body JSON is 95 UTF-8 bytes.
Supply 100 such entries. The actual component produces 100 img elements; the JSON is 8,213 UTF-8 bytes, demonstrating there is no aggregate preview-count gate.

Separately stream 12,000 zero-valued 1-bit grayscale scanlines of 1,501 bytes each through zlib, count and discard compressed output. 18,012,000 filtered bytes compress to 17,525 bytes; with 57 bytes of normal PNG chunk/signature overhead this would be 17,582 bytes or 23,444 Base64 characters. This is far below the MCP 1,400,000-character and 2 MiB body caps, although a 12,000x12,000 RGBA raster is 576,000,000 bytes. No complete image was constructed or decoded.
findings.recommendation: Use the shared strict byte/signature/dimension validation before creating any media URL. Make image loading an explicit per-item action and bound simultaneous/aggregate preview resources, with useful rejection feedback and cleanup on release/owner changes. Preserve the original result receipt and raw JSON download path independently of preview eligibility.

validations.detail: 17 HTTP/WebSocket authorization/admission/slow-response tests, 3 worker-connection ownership tests and 13 durable operation recovery tests. Local fixtures only.

Loaded unmodified current TSX/TS via Vite SSR, rendered static HTML, and counted streamed compression output without a raster decoder. First header-only run and final compression-count run both exited 0.
Initial and final global snapshot both match the assigned frozen digest; final verification performed immediately before report generation.
Computed SHA-256 of each assigned file and compared with reviewer start baseline; all 198 match.

One assignment metadata lookup used files instead of names and returned empty output; corrected before coverage. One rg call using a Windows path wildcard failed with invalid filename syntax; rerun against explicit current paths. A TypeScript transpileModule capability check returned undefined (the installed package exposes no such API); the probe used Vite SSR successfully. Tool output truncations were followed by complete supplementary source reads. A later verbose test-report display was truncated; parsed totals and all non-passing results were read separately (zero failures/skips). No setup error was treated as a passing validation.

No full test suite, aggregate target or all-JS selection, production build/typecheck, interactive browser, native Linux PTY/service, provider/model, real MCP, remote SSH, login or external integration execution. Only the specifically listed targeted tests and safe local probe ran.

limitations: Complete means the assigned 198-file inspection is complete; it is not a clean audit because one confirmed P2 remains unfixed.
No source, test, feature-evidence, configuration or documentation file was modified. Only ignored reviewer helpers and this audit report were written; capability coverage was not regenerated.

Assigned web/VERIFICATION.md contains historical audit prose. It was inspected as assigned documentation only; its claims were not relied upon and no linked prior audit reports, old implementation, sibling code or repository history were inspected.

The synthetic PNG header is intentionally incomplete and cannot establish a browser-decoder crash. The additional compression-size count establishes feasibility below serialized caps without constructing or decoding a complete oversized image. No actual memory exhaustion, browser crash or graphics-decoder behavior was tested.
Static full-file review and 33 selected tests cannot prove all browser/platform integrations. Unexecuted categories are explicitly retained in V6.
No personal CODEX_HOME, credentials, paid calls, provider/model requests, live MCP service, login, SSH or external network service was accessed.

The reviewer baseline helper contains an early manually entered 17:14:30 timestamp; this report instead uses the actual observed baseline command time 17:14:49.065Z as startedAt. Hash contents of that baseline were used only for file-integrity comparison.
